newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says could turn to Asia over row with EU.
newsitem.headline: Iran says could turn to Asia over row with EU.

text.p: Iranian state radio said on Thursday that Iran could turn from the European Union to Asia for its trade because of a row over a German court's ruling that accused Tehran leaders of ordering political killings.

"Iran has other choices (besides Europe) such as developing relations with Asian countries and could, if necessary, decrease its dealings with Europe and increase them with Asia," state-run Tehran radio said in a commentary.
The radio said this could happen if EU states did not follow a policy independent of the United States and Israel -- Iran's arch-enemies -- which it blamed for the current dispute.
It was commenting about the diplomatic row caused by the court verdict last week that said top Iranian leaders ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the slayings, which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.

The radio said Iran had followed a policy of establishing ties with most world states to minimise its vulnerability and was able to overcome any difficulties caused by a disruption of relations with EU countries.

"Therefore America and Zionist circles should not be under the false impression that they can cause trouble for the Islamic Republic of Iran by instigating problems in Iran's ties with Europe," the radio said.
EU ambassadors to Iran briefed EU officials on Thursday on Tehran's reaction to their withdrawal last week and to the end of the bloc's policy of trying to bring Iran closer to the West.
Iran has responded to the recalling for consultations of all European Union ambassadors, except Greece's, by announcing it would reciprocate.
